Development guide

Tech Scan: Stack views

Use these views to connect an existing application stack to the component decisions that shape an AI-assisted delivery system.

These cross-cutting indexes are not runtime components. They point to the owning references rather than repeating product catalogues. Draft research, not locally validated.

On this page
LanguagesAWS platformSources

Languages: start with the existing application

The engineering lead should first record the application language, build and deployment target, team expertise and the constraints of its existing estate. Choose a new language only when a specific requirement justifies the migration and the team can operate it. React is a user-interface framework, not a language; a React application can use JavaScript or TypeScript.

  • Java: retain the existing service and build unless a demonstrated need changes the choice. Ask for language-appropriate test, mutation and architecture checks in Verification; connect their results to Delivery.
  • TypeScript or JavaScript, including React: identify whether the change is in the browser, server or both; select checks and release evidence for each boundary in Verification and Delivery.
  • Python: use the same evidence and operating checks for an existing Python service or an agent integration; compare its dependencies and execution environment with the Harness and Sandbox references.

Do not infer the application language from the agent or SDK language. The application, agent integration and deployment pipeline can have different languages. Record the chosen stack, test command, owner and unresolved compatibility gaps before piloting; return to the relevant component reference for the actual tooling decision.

AWS platform: trace the request and evidence

Use AWS as the starting platform, not as a substitute for required capability, approved data handling, identity, security and an operating owner. A team should record the following path for its actual account and workload before adopting it:

  1. Model, endpoint and region: start with the approved managed Claude or OpenAI route through Bedrock; take direct-provider access through the applicable exception process. Record the model, operation, endpoint, source region and every possible destination region, including fallback. An inference profile can route to a different destination region; inspect its actual destinations before accepting it.[1] Use Models and access and Gateway for the route and controls.
  2. Network and identity: map the user, workload role, resources, outbound destinations and enforcement points. Test allowed and denied access. A VPC-connected AgentCore Runtime or built-in tool has no internet access by default; a public subnet alone does not provide it.[2] Network access is not identity authorisation, and a gateway cannot enforce traffic that bypasses it. See Sandbox boundaries, Gateway and Harness.
  3. Retention and retrieval: trace prompts, responses, logs, retrieved records and stored memory separately. Check the selected endpoint, account setting, model and destination region; AWS documents differing retention modes; for cross-region profiles it notes that prompts and outputs may be stored in opt-in destination regions for abuse detection.[3][1] Set and test deletion, access and retention for each store; see Context.
  4. Work and release: select the agent and workflow for the task, then carry verification results into the release record. The Agents and Workflows and factories references cover work through a proposed change; Verification supplies evidence, and Delivery addresses release and operations. Verification evidence alone does not authorise release.

Ask the engineering and platform owners to test the exact model operation, failed authorisation, egress and retention configuration in the intended account. Keep the configuration, results, decision owner and unresolved gaps with the adoption record. If a required boundary cannot be demonstrated, resolve it before use rather than assuming AWS preference overrides it.

Next, choose the owning reference above and compare its options against the recorded constraint; revisit the decision when the stack or provider configuration changes.

These provider documents describe service behaviour, not local validation, organisational approval or every model and region. Recheck the actual configuration before adoption.

Sources

References last checked: 14 November 2026.

  1. AWS, Supported Regions and models for inference profiles. Explains source and destination regions; availability depends on the chosen model and profile. Used in AWS platform.
  2. AWS, Configure AgentCore Runtime and tools for VPC. Describes connectivity for VPC-connected Runtime and built-in tools, not every application network. Used in AWS platform.
  3. AWS, Data retention. Describes endpoint and model-dependent retention; it does not establish retention for the team's logs or other stores. Used in AWS platform.
